title: Probe trust fallback and regional derating controller
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: We observe autoscaler thrash and cross-region failover cascades when a subset of health probes spike (usually during brief GC events, kernel preemption, or network blips). Current readiness/liveness signals are binary and treated equally by the autoscaler and traffic router; noisy probes cause premature capacity reductions, regional circuit breakers trip too aggressively, and SLOs (p50 latency and p99 tail) are violated for customer-facing routes.

Goal: Build a lightweight probe-trust scoring layer and a regional derating controller that: (1) computes a per-pool probe trust score using historical probe behavior and request-shape metrics, (2) applies soft derating of autoscaler decisions rather than hard scale-to-zero behavior, (3) integrates with circuit-breaker policies to prefer graceful load-shedding and local fallback model variants before cross-region failover, and (4) exposes observability and rollout controls in Console.

Scope: Implementation covers the probe-trust evaluator, an autoscaler policy plugin (soft-derate window + EWMA smoothing), an integration adapter for the regional circuit-breaker controller, and dashboards/alerting. Not in scope: model-level fallback policies (separate PRD) and billing changes.

Key design points:
- Probe trust metric: 0..100 integer computed per-instance and aggregated to pool using weighted EWMA. Weight inputs: recent readiness failures, recovery rate, tail latency delta, and request QPS shape histogram.
- Soft derate policy: instead of immediate pod eviction on readiness failure, we bias the autoscaler’s target scale by trust-weighted confidence. Low trust -> increase safety margin and extend grace window; high trust -> normal behavior.
- Circuit integration: when regional availability drops below threshold, prefer local derate + model-variant fallback for a short grace period before initiating cross-region routing. This reduces network egress and SLO violation blast radius.
- Observability: new per-pool 'probe-trust' timeseries, derate events audit trail, and a Console toggle for canary rollout.

Tradeoffs & considerations:
- Complexity vs benefit: introduces extra smoothing and heuristics. Mitigations: default conservative settings, opt-in via rollout, and strong telemetry to revert quickly.
- Latency of detection: EWMA smoothing reduces false positives but increases time-to-detect real failures. We tune half-life and derate windows to balance SLOs.
- Safety: ensure we never permanently hide genuine outage signals; circuit-breaker will still open after sustained degraded health with confirmed request errors.
comments: 2026-01-29 - Liam Chen: Created ticket after postmortem for incident 2026-01-26 where regional autoscaler oscillation caused >2m p99 spikes for customers in eu-west. Initial investigation found >30% of readiness failures were short lived (<12s) and correlated with kernel preemption in older instance types.

2026-02-03 - Ayesha Kapoor: Spike simulation harness added to repo (sim/synth-probe-noise). Ran 1000 simulated failure traces across 3 regions; baseline autoscaler flapped in 18% of runs leading to unnecessary cross-region failover. Proposed EWMA half-life of 45s as starting point.

2026-02-10 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Reviewed design. Concern: EWMA may mask correlated infra outages. Decision: add an 'escalation detector' that bypasses trust scoring when request error ratio exceeds 1% sustained for 60s.

2026-02-18 - Design review: UX approved a small Console affordance to expose derate factor and manual override per-customer. PM requested audit log of derate decisions for compliance. Added requirement for audit entries to include causation tags.

2026-02-25 - Patch: Implemented probe-trust evaluator and unit tests. PR: runtime/pull/7890. Load tests show 62% reduction in autoscaler target churn in synthetic noise scenarios. Identified bug where weight normalization could overflow on extreme histograms; fixed in PR.

2026-03-05 - Canary: Rolling canary to internal canary org (canary region: us-west-2). Observed one flapping group; adjusted derate window from 120s to 90s. No customer-impacting SLO regressions so far.

2026-03-12 - Next: Prepare runbook addition for on-call SRE to diagnose probe-trust vs real outage, and add alerting: (A) probe-trust drop >40% for >2m, (B) derate events >5 in 10m for pool -> page on-call. Schedule broader rollout pending validation (target 2026-03-29).
